name: Hal Jackman
current_role: Patriarch / largest family shareholder of E-L Financial Corporation (Toronto); former Lieutenant Governor of Ontario
profile: Henry N.R. 'Hal' Jackman (b. 1932) expanded the insurance and investment empire built by his father Harry Jackman, chairing National Trust and Empire Life; the family controls TSX-listed E-L Financial, now run by his son Duncan. He was Ontario's 25th Lieutenant Governor (1991-97) and U of T chancellor (1997-2003). In 2025 he gave $80M to U of T law, renamed the Henry N.R. Jackman Faculty of Law.
interesting_fact: His September 2025 $80 million gift was the largest ever to a Canadian law school, bringing his giving to U of T's law faculty to $100 million; the school was renamed the Henry N.R. Jackman Faculty of Law.
deep_cut_fact: While Lieutenant Governor in 1991, Jackman donated his historic collection of toy soldiers (over 650 figures) to the Royal Ontario Museum; he also served as honorary colonel of the Governor General's Horse Guards, a Toronto militia unit.
notes: Aged 94; no personal public channels. E-L Financial press releases name CFO Scott F. Ewert as the contact (published business line (416) 947-2578). Honorary-colonel detail from U of T/Victoria College sources: https://vic.utoronto.ca/henry-n-r-jackman-honoured-with-international-business-lnew-news-page

name: NR Narayana Murthy
current_role: Founder and Chairman Emeritus, Infosys; founder of family investment firm Catamaran Ventures
profile: N.R. Narayana Murthy (b. 1946) co-founded Infosys in 1981 with six colleagues, seeded by Rs 10,000 from his wife Sudha Murty, and built it into one of India's largest IT services companies, serving as CEO and chairman. Often called the father of the Indian IT sector, he is now Chairman Emeritus and invests via Catamaran Ventures.
interesting_fact: He has said being arrested and expelled near the Yugoslav-Bulgarian border in 1974, while hitchhiking back from Europe, turned him from a 'confused leftist' into a 'compassionate capitalist'.
deep_cut_fact: Before Infosys, as chief systems programmer at IIM Ahmedabad he worked on India's first time-sharing computer system and designed a BASIC interpreter for ECIL; his first startup, Softronics, folded after about a year and a half.
notes: Infosys press email reaches the company, not him directly; Catamaran Ventures (his family office, catamaranventures.com) may be a more direct route but no published email was verified. Gives frequent public lectures and interviews, often on work ethic and entrepreneurship.
